investigation.title: local-agent-runtime eval failure: upstream model provider returned 424 provider_account_unavailable, causing 502 on POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test
investigation.summary: The local-agent-runtime eval check failed because the AURA backend returned HTTP 502 wrapping a 424 Failed Dependency from the upstream model provider, with error code provider_account_unavailable. Because the runtime test call never completed successfully, the eval runner received no response payload and all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are absent, causing a full contract validation failure.
investigation.rootCause: The upstream model provider was temporarily unreachable from the AURA backend at the time the eval ran (2026-10-02T13:41:36–42Z). The backend surfaced this as a 424 Failed Dependency with code provider_account_unavailable, which the harness translated into a 502 bad_gateway response to the eval runner. Because the LLM call never returned, the runtime test endpoint produced no response body, leaving all five required evidence fields unpopulated and failing the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json (lines 102–105). This is an eval infrastructure failure reflecting a transient upstream provider availability event; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident is present in the packet.

possibleCauses: Primary: Transient upstream model provider outage or rate-limit event at the time of the eval run, causing the AURA backend to return 424 provider_account_unavailable and surface it as 502 to the eval harness. Supported by the explicit provider error message and the fact that sibling checks (agent creation, permissions) passed without issue.

Secondary: A provider account or API key configuration issue on the AURA backend side (e.g., expired credentials, quota exhaustion, or account suspension for the eval service account). The error message explicitly states 'This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits,' which points toward a backend-to-provider connectivity or account state problem rather than a caller credential issue.

Tertiary: A transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the AURA backend and the model provider endpoint at the moment of the eval run. This would produce the same 424/502 error chain and would be self-healing on retry.

investigation.title: Project Agent Chat Stream Eval Failure: HTTP 424 provider_account_unavailable Blocks Session Persistence and Text Generation
investigation.summary: The desktop-release eval for project-agent-chat-stream failed at 2026-10-02T13:41:57Z with an HTTP 424 Failed Dependency error (code: provider_account_unavailable, support_id=7d38ef271d09), meaning the AURA backend could not reach the upstream model provider during the eval run. Because the model provider was unreachable, the agent stream emitted an error frame instead of text_delta frames, leaving textSample empty and preventing session persistence, which caused sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase to never be populated — failing three of the nine required evidence assertions defined in the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The upstream model provider was temporarily unavailable from AURA's backend at the time of the eval run (2026-10-02T13:41:47–13:41:57Z). The API returned HTTP 424 with error code provider_account_unavailable (support_id=7d38ef271d09). This caused the project/session chat stream to terminate with an error frame before any text_delta, text content, or session persistence could occur, directly producing the missing evidence: sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase. This is an eval-time infrastructure dependency failure, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; impact is scoped to this observability eval run.

investigation.title: Project Agent Workflows: All Checks Failing Due to HTTP 424 provider_account_unavailable on Desktop Release
investigation.summary: Every check in the project-agent-workflows feature (session-share-public-read, project-agent-chat-stream, project-agent-tool-roundtrip, project-agent-a2a-roundtrip, project-agent-subagent-roundtrip) failed on desktop-release at 2026-10-02T13:41–13:44Z. All chat-turn-dependent checks received an HTTP 424 Failed Dependency with error code provider_account_unavailable before any session, share, or tool evidence could be produced, causing the eval runner to halt and leave sessionId, shareIdPresent, shareUrlPresent, and publicMessageCount absent from the collected evidence.
investigation.rootCause: The upstream model provider was unreachable from the AURA backend at the time of the eval run. The API returned HTTP 424 with error code provider_account_unavailable and the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This caused runProjectChatTurn (called at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1848) to return a FAIL status immediately, which the runner propagated via the early-exit guard at line 1849 (if chat.status === CHECK_STATUS.FAIL return chat), preventing all downstream steps — session creation, share-link generation, and public-read verification — from executing. The failure is localized to the eval infrastructure's dependency on the model provider API; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Project Agent A2A Roundtrip Eval Failure: Planner Agent Emits Error Frames Instead of Tool Calls; Model Provider Unavailable Across All Project-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: The project-agent-a2a-roundtrip eval failed on desktop-release (desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64) because the planner agent never invoked list_agents or send_to_agent — toolNames is empty, listAgentsUsed and sendToAgentUsed are both false, and the reviewer agent received zero events before timing out after 120 000 ms. All four sibling checks under project-agent-workflows also failed in the same run window, with two of them (project-agent-chat-stream and session-share-public-read) returning HTTP 424 provider_account_unavailable errors, strongly suggesting the model provider was unreachable at the time of the run, which prevented the planner from generating any tool calls and caused the entire A2A roundtrip to stall.
investigations.rootCause: The model provider was unavailable (HTTP 424 provider_account_unavailable, code "provider_account_unavailable") during the eval window, preventing the planner agent from producing any tool-call turns. Without a list_agents call the planner could not discover the reviewer, without a send_to_agent call no message was routed, and the reviewer event stream timed out after 120 000 ms with zero events. This is an eval-infrastructure / upstream-dependency failure observed in the desktop-release runtime environment; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

This caused the project/session chat stream to terminate with an error frame before any text_delta, text content, or session persistence could occur, directly producing the missing evidence: sessionId, sessionCount, and expectedPhrase.
